groups.name: Agriculture sector
groups.blurb: Land, water and what grows on it — where acreage, yield and price realisation are the levers a district can actually move.

sectors.title: Crops (Agriculture)
sectors.estimation: Estimated using district crop area and production from state departments. Covers grains, cereals, pulses, oilseeds, sugarcane, cotton, fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices, etc. (Horticulture estimated separately on area & production of fruits/vegetables/spices/flowers.)
actions: Prepare district crop strategies; facilitate early adoption by large farmers
Expand coverage of high-yielding & climate-smart seeds; ensure timely distribution
Monitor fertilizer supply chains at block level to prevent seasonal shortages
Widen soil-health-card coverage and farmer advisories
Track PM Fasal Bima Yojana claim-settlement ratio; use digital crop survey for acreage/pest tracking
Hand-hold FPOs, link them to processing units and markets
Build product identity (GI tagging, branding) and facilitate export certifications
policies: National Mission on Agricultural Extension & Technology

sectors.title: Livestock & Fisheries
sectors.estimation: Estimated using district production & prices of milk, eggs, meat, wool (State Animal Husbandry Dept + Livestock Census) and fish/silk/honey from concerned departments. Aquaculture is a major AP strength.
actions: Expand artificial insemination & sex-sorted semen coverage; promote high-yield indigenous breeds and high-value fish species
Monitor vaccination supply chain & coverage; track livestock insurance claims ratio
Expand para-vet doorstep services; popularise livestock health & pond hygiene
Build cold-chain / chilling / insulated transport to cut post-harvest loss
Promote processing units (paneer, yoghurt, fish fillets) and cluster-based logistics
FPOs for collective harvesting & pooling; urban retail linkages
GI tagging / branding and export certifications

sectors.title: Forestry & Logging
sectors.estimation: Estimated from district prices and production (Major & Minor Forest Produce) by the State Forest Department; trees-outside-forests apportioned using forest & geographical area. Fuelwood from NSS consumption survey + population projections.
actions: Expand green cover via plantation & restoration of degraded land; monitor sapling availability and plantation targets
Coordinate fire prevention/control with modern monitoring tools
Enforce against illegal felling & encroachment
Ensure timely recording of timber extraction & transit permits at depots
Support local processing (bamboo furniture, resin) via MSME & skilling schemes

groups.name: Industry sector
groups.blurb: Extracting, making and building — where formalisation, power reliability and capital works convert into measurable value added. Includes mining, which the state classification counts here rather than with agriculture.

sectors.title: Mining & Quarrying
sectors.estimation: State GVA apportioned to districts on district-wise mineral production. Major minerals from IBM; minor minerals & sand from the Directorate of Geology & Mining.
actions: Support site exploration via coordinated local surveys & transparent resource data
Push for timely auctions/permits by the state mining department
Curb illegal mining & mineral transport; establish regulated corridors and check-posts
Promote mechanisation (brick kilns, stone cutting, granite polishing)
Improve quarry access & supply-chain infra (weighbridges, warehouses)
Common Facility Centres for branding, quality certification & marketing for small processors
policies: MSME cluster schemes for mineral processing

sectors.title: Manufacturing
sectors.estimation: Organised manufacturing GVA from district-level ASI data (≈two-thirds of total). Remaining organised + unorganised GVA allocated to districts using relevant activity indicators (electricity, GST, employment).
actions: Maintain a dynamic land bank with ready-to-allot plots (with IDAs); fast-track land-use conversion
Ensure reliable power/water/waste management with last-mile connectivity
Promote cluster facilities: CFCs, design/testing labs, branding centres
Ease access to bank credit, subsidies, guarantee schemes; support investors via Udyami Mitras
Maintain relationships with top firms; expedite their concerns
Work with DIEPC on vendor databases & MSME registration; streamline expansion approvals

sectors.title: Electricity, Gas, Water & Utilities
sectors.estimation: State GVA apportioned using weighted indicators: electricity consumption/generation/transmission (primary), biogas plants, LPG sales, water-supply emoluments, Har Ghar Jal tap connections, Swachh Bharat (R&U) expenditure.
actions: Expand household/industrial/agri connections via DISCOMs, Jal Jeevan Mission, gas distributors
Drive enrolment for universal electricity, piped water and PNG where networks exist
Monitor service quality (power hours, water pressure, gas availability); resolve bottlenecks
Fast-track maintenance, metering and feeder separation
Cut losses via efficient pumps, LED adoption, stronger billing & collections; promote recycling & renewables (rooftop solar, biogas, mini-grids)
policies: AP Clean Energy / Renewable Energy Policy

sectors.title: Construction
sectors.estimation: State GVA apportioned using weighted indicators: emoluments of local-body/PWD workers, MGNREGA person-days, BOCW workers, PMAY (R&U) expenditure, GST from cement & steel.
actions: Identify & initiate new public works (roads, housing, irrigation, urban infra) with PWD/ULBs/line departments
Track project pipelines; fast-track sanctioning of viable proposals
Improve material quality to raise Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF)
Reduce turnaround time: fast-track clearances, monitor contractors, resolve on-ground bottlenecks
policies: AP Building & Other Construction Workers (BOCW) welfare

groups.name: Services sector
groups.blurb: Trade, movement, finance and human capital — the fastest growing share of most district economies.

sectors.title: Trade, Hotels & Restaurants (Tourism)
sectors.estimation: State GVA apportioned to districts on weighted activity indicators (trade & repair ~87%: commodity GVA, GST; hotels & restaurants: tourist arrivals).
actions: Identify & prioritise 2–3 anchor tourism sites for focused development
Register heritage buildings/crafts (ASI Act) to drive preservation & tourism
Promote local fairs, festivals, sports events; coordinate with state tourism boards
Link tourism clusters with ODOP, handicrafts, MSMEs; facilitate investment under AP Tourism Policy
Upgrade sites (amenities, last-mile access with PWD/transport); train guides & hospitality workers
Attract PPP/CSR investment; enforce hygiene, safety & fair pricing

sectors.title: Transport, Storage & Communication
sectors.estimation: State GVA apportioned on: railway track length, registered commercial vehicles, air passengers, bus permits, petrol/CNG/diesel sales, district storage capacity, BTS towers, sector workforce.
actions: Improve local connectivity (rural roads, bus stands) for passenger & freight movement
Promote district markets for freight aggregation
Expedite permissions for telecom towers, fibre rollout
Ensure timely completion of key transport projects (roads, depots, logistics hubs)
Facilitate land & approvals for warehouses, cold storage, bus/truck terminals

sectors.title: Financial Services
sectors.estimation: State GVA apportioned on district-wise credit amount, deposit amount and number of bank branches.
pathways: Improve credit access, CD ratio & annual credit plan
actions: Use district coordination forums (DCC/DLCC) to push wider banking coverage in underserved pockets
Ensure registration of financial companies present in the district
Support alternative access points: ATMs/digital kiosks, bank mitras, post offices
Run loan camps for KCC, Mudra, SVANidhi; review priority-sector-lending targets
Maintain a healthy credit-deposit (CD) ratio and reduce NPAs; promote digital payments
Coordinate financial-literacy drives for schools, SHGs, farmers

sectors.title: Real Estate, Dwellings & Professional Services
sectors.estimation: State GSVA apportioned on weighted activity indicators. Includes real-estate company revenues, imputed rental value of dwellings, and professional/IT services (software exports via STPI).
actions: Accelerate property registration & mutation via digitisation at district registrars
Strengthen RERA implementation; faster dispute resolution
Expand stamp-duty & property registration drives to widen the tax base
Support affordable housing (PMAY, state schemes) with ULBs & housing boards
Improve property-tax collections via updated assessments & technology
Promote registration of local professionals (lawyers, accountants, IT firms); ensure STPI registration of IT units; link to startup/skilling schemes
indicators: Real Estate, Dwellings & Professional Services GVA

sectors.title: Public Administration & Defence
sectors.estimation: Apportioned on salaries & emoluments of state government employees (from treasury) and of local bodies & state autonomous institutions. Defence is centrally managed (no district role).
actions: Fill vacant positions through timely recruitment & promotions
Maintain an updated list of autonomous institutions (central & state) for accurate estimation
Promote digital systems to improve operational efficiency
Strengthen grievance-redressal systems; organise staff training to improve service delivery

sectors.title: Other Services (Education & Health)
sectors.estimation: Apportioned on indicators such as teachers in govt/aided schools, GST from coaching institutes, private polytechnics (Education); and GST from hospitals, NHM expenditure (Health). Private & unincorporated components from MCA21 & NSS.
actions: Facilitate clearances for private providers (schools, hospitals, diagnostics) to expand capacity
Engage private/vocational institutes in District Skill Committees; map demand to priority sectors
Track faculty/health-worker deployment; escalate vacancies for timely recruitment
Continue enrolment & transition drives; monitor mid-day meals, scholarships, uniforms/textbooks
Build confidence in public health facilities (punctuality, ASHA/ANM incentives, outreach camps); monitor care-quality parameters

method.title: How to read your district in 4 steps
steps: Look at GDDP, rank, growth and per-capita income in the district map.
Compare each sector's share in your district with its share in the state. Where your share is higher, you likely have an edge (a Location Quotient above 1).
Understand how that GVA is created
and which pathways raise it — yield, acreage, price realisation, formalisation — using the sector playbooks below.
Pick the administrative levers you control,
attach a scheme and a monitoring indicator, and act.

leverage.title: The district officer's leverage
points: You cannot manage what you cannot measure.
GVA gives a sector-by-sector scorecard for your district.
Doubling down on a sector where you already lead is faster than building one from scratch.
Timely seed delivery, a faster land-use approval, a cold-chain link — each adds measurable GVA.
The NITI for States portal and AI tools surface what comparable districts did.

ai_tools: Find case studies; draw insights from best practices across districts/states
“What innovative steps did districts in India take to raise farm incomes / boost MSMEs / grow tourism?”
Draft district strategy notes, summarise schemes, brainstorm levers per sector
“Act as an economist. Given my district is strong in aquaculture but weak in processing, list 8 levers a Collector can pull.”
Curated case studies & good practices across Agriculture, MSMEs, Manufacturing, Skilling, Tourism
Browse by sector → filter by state → adapt to district context
Track high-frequency indicators (Vahan, e-NAM, NREGA, Udyam, GST)
Set monthly review of sector indicators in DRC/DLCC meetings
niti: Search the NITI for States portal (nitiforstates.gov.in) by sector to find what comparable districts/states did — then adapt, don't copy.
Agriculture & Allied: how did high-aquaculture districts move up the value chain into processing & exports?
MSME & Manufacturing: which districts used ODOP + cluster CFCs to formalise unorganised units?
Tourism: how did districts convert a single anchor site into multi-day stays and higher per-tourist spend?
Skilling & Livelihoods: how were District Skill Committees used to match training to local priority sectors?
